stories.title: Russia plans to mobilise 600,000 troops this year and next, Ukraine says
stories.summary: Ukrainian intelligence said Moscow has already decided to call up 300,000 this year and 300,000 in 2027, driven by massive losses and a collapse in voluntary recruitment. Kyiv expects the announcement to come after September's elections.

stories.title: Over 90,000 affected by Himalayan landslide, Red Cross says
stories.summary: More than 90,000 people are estimated to be directly affected by the Himalayan landslide and in urgent need of humanitarian assistance, the Red Cross said on Friday, as aid officials voiced fears of further flooding. "We believe that at least 93,000 people have been affected and are in great need," David Fisher, head of delegation for the International Federation of Red Cross and Red Crescent Societies in Nepal, told a Geneva press briefing. "We're of course very concerned about the secondary flood," he added. Fisher said that the organisation's trucks with relief supplies were blocked after a lake formed by the landslide broke its banks, temporarily halting rescue operations. Kamal Kishore, Head of the United Nations Office for Disaster Risk Reduction, warned of further "cascading hazards that might unfold". "In a sense, the disaster is not yet completely over. It is still unfolding in some ways," he said. World Health Organization spokesperson Tarik Jasarevic said at the same briefing that six health facilities had been damaged in the landslide and that eight healthcare workers were missing.

stories.title: (LEAD) S. Korean rescue teams struggling to reach Nepal flood site as 9 remain missing
stories.summary: SEOUL, Aug. 28 (Yonhap) -- South Korean government and corporate response teams ...
article_sentences: South Korean government and corporate response teams are struggling to reach a hydropower plant construction site in Nepal where nine South Koreans remain unaccounted for amid concerns over further flooding, officials said Friday.
The government's joint rapid response team arrived in Kathmandu late Thursday, while corporate response teams from Doosan Enerbility Co.
and Korea South-East Power Co.
arrived early Friday.

The government and the companies have secured a total of six helicopters for search and rescue operations, but the aircraft have yet to receive flight approval from Nepalese authorities, according to ministry officials.
"Helicopter travel is essential to reach the area, as roads and bridges have been washed away.
But Nepalese authorities have restricted private helicopter operations over concerns about the possibility of additional flooding," a ministry oficial said.

The nine missing people -- six employees of Doosan and three of the power generation firm -- were working at a construction site in Rasuwa district when a massive flash flood and mudslide struck the area Wednesday morning.
They had been staying in offices and accommodations in a relatively low-lying area, many of which are believed to have been swept away by the flooding.
Families of the missing workers urged the government to quickly send helicopters to the site, saying nearly 48 hours had passed since the disaster.
"Our only request is to get the helicopters flying as soon as possible," family members said at a press briefing Friday.
"We believe today is the golden time.
